key_insight: Counterfactual bias in open-source LLMs for pediatric triage varies widely across models and does not reliably improve with larger size or medical-domain pretraining.
clinical_relevance: For ED triage support, models can shift acuity ratings when only demographic or contextual details change, creating fairness and safety risks even when the clinical vignette is unchanged.
method: Paired clinical vignettes were created by changing one non-clinical variable at a time while keeping the presentation fixed.
Ten open-source LLMs were compared, including general, medical-domain, and fine-tuned Qwen, MedGemma, MedLLaMA2, and GPT-OSS models.
Outputs were scored for any shift, undertriage, overtriage, >1 ESI-level shifts, mean shift, and mean absolute shift.
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s evaluation set, the fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B had the lowest any-shift rate (5.27%) and mean absolute shift (0.0534), versus 16.02% and 0.1706 for the base model.
watch_item: Counterfactual audits reveal sensitivity patterns, but they do not by themselves prove real-world clinical impact or guarantee fairness in deployment.
paper_title: Counterfactual Auditing of Bias in Open-Source Large Language Models for Clinical Triage
